Mary Lee (Suffragist) — Who she was: An Irish-born social justice campaigner who moved to Adelaide, South Australia, in 1879. [Australian Dictionary of Biography +2] Key achievement: She co-founded the South Australian Women's Suffrage League in 1888. Historical impact: Her leadership led to the Constitution Amendment Act of 1894, which made South Australia the second place in the world to give women the right to vote and the first to allow them to run for parliament. Other work: She also advocated for better working conditions, helping run the Working Women's Trade Union... [The Australian Women's Register +2]

- Mary Lee (singer) (1921–2022): A Scottish variety singer and broadcaster famous for performing with British dance bands during the 1930s. [Wikipedia]
